provenance.notes: This is the pre-consensus generation, retained only so legacy free text can be ingested without guessing. The claim tokens SP/CP(component)/MO/CL are the ones actually used in TableS9 sheet 2 and in the EN.docx section 3, 6 and 8 text. The EN.docx section 2 table had already been rewritten to SC/SI/CP while its section 4 evidence table still carried the working markers 'CX or CO?' and 'OS?SS?'; the tokens SM, HO and UN are therefore recorded here with status proposed, and OS is not part of this version at all. Superseded by smb-v2-consensus on 2026-09-03.

annotation_level.label: Confirmed structure
annotation_level.definition_source: Schymanski et al. (2014), Identifying small molecules via high resolution mass spectrometry: communicating confidence. Environmental Science & Technology.
annotation_level.notes: The proposal enumerates the level and cites the scale; it does not restate the level criteria.

annotation_level.label: Probable structure
annotation_level.definition_source: Schymanski et al. (2014), Identifying small molecules via high resolution mass spectrometry: communicating confidence. Environmental Science & Technology.
annotation_level.notes: The proposal enumerates the level and cites the scale; it does not restate the level criteria.

annotation_level.label: Tentative candidate
annotation_level.definition: Tentative candidate. Level 3 records are further qualified by a level3_claim tag.
annotation_level.definition_source: Schymanski et al. (2014), Identifying small molecules via high resolution mass spectrometry: communicating confidence. Environmental Science & Technology.
annotation_level.notes: Only this level accepts a claim tag.

annotation_level.label: Unequivocal molecular formula
annotation_level.definition_source: Schymanski et al. (2014), Identifying small molecules via high resolution mass spectrometry: communicating confidence. Environmental Science & Technology.
annotation_level.notes: The proposal enumerates the level and cites the scale; it does not restate the level criteria.

annotation_level.label: Exact mass
annotation_level.definition_source: Schymanski et al. (2014), Identifying small molecules via high resolution mass spectrometry: communicating confidence. Environmental Science & Technology.
annotation_level.notes: The proposal enumerates the level and cites the scale; it does not restate the level criteria.

level3_claim.label: Structure proposed
level3_claim.definition: A single two-dimensional constitutional structure is proposed, but not confirmed by a reference standard.

level3_claim.label: Component proposed
level3_claim.definition: Defined molecular components, building blocks, or modifications are proposed, but their positions, connectivities, or arrangements remain unresolved.
level3_claim.notes: HAZARD: this token is re-bound. In smb-v2-consensus CP means class proposed (smb:claim/class). Migrates to SC.

level3_claim.label: Motif proposed
level3_claim.definition: A diagnostic substructure or structural motif is proposed, but a component-level representation is not sufficiently defined.

level3_claim.label: Class proposed
level3_claim.definition: The annotation is limited to a chemical or metabolite class.
level3_claim.notes: Migrates to CP in smb-v2-consensus, which is why the token CP is re-bound.

evidence.label: Reference standard evidence
evidence.definition: Confirms Level 1 identity using an authentic standard measured under comparable or identical conditions.

evidence.label: Formula / mass evidence
evidence.definition: Supports molecular formula or mass consistency.

evidence.label: Spectral library evidence
evidence.definition: Supports structure/class by matching to an experimental MS/MS library or literature spectrum.
evidence.notes: score_convention is mandatory for stored scores because MS-DIAL reports squared cosines while the criteria are written as dot products.

evidence.label: Diagnostic fragment evidence
evidence.definition: Supports substructure, motif, class, or structure using diagnostic ions, neutral losses, or fragmentation patterns.

evidence.label: Ion mobility evidence
evidence.definition: Supports annotation through ion mobility, drift time, or CCS.

evidence.label: In silico evidence
evidence.definition: Supports formula, class, motif, or structure using computational annotation.

evidence.label: Molecular networking evidence
evidence.definition: Supports structural relationship using spectral similarity networks and interpretable mass shifts.

evidence.label: Spectral Similarity
evidence.definition: Spectral Similarity to related molecule, e.g. between Molecular Network neighbours.
evidence.notes: Contested and dropped from smb-v2-consensus. No counterpart concept exists in the consensus set, so a reading carrying this concept cannot be migrated without loss.

evidence.label: Homologue evidence
evidence.definition: Kendrick mass defect, homologue series evidence.

evidence.label: Contextual evidence
evidence.definition: Supports annotation using biological, biosynthetic, taxonomic, pathway, sample, diet, perturbation, or organism context.
evidence.notes: Renamed to CO in smb-v2-consensus. The EN.docx section 4 row was still marked 'CX or CO?'.

evidence.label: Unclassified additional evidence
evidence.definition: Other evidence - UV detector, IR, fragmentation, 2D chromatography.

combination_rules.note: Default for a single two-dimensional structure.
combination_rules.source_text_verbatim: SP is normally reported without CL because a proposed 2D structure generally determines the corresponding chemical class under the classification system used.

combination_rules.note: Reserved for exceptional cases where class assignment depends on stereochemical, configurational, or ontology-specific distinctions that are not fully represented by the reported structure.
combination_rules.source_text_verbatim: SP+CL is reserved for exceptional cases where class assignment depends on stereochemical, configurational, or ontology-specific distinctions that are not fully represented by the reported structure.

combination_rules.note: Allowed when class-level information provides independent useful metadata.
combination_rules.source_text_verbatim: CL may be appended to CP or MO when class-level information provides independent useful metadata.

combination_rules.note: Allowed when class-level information provides independent useful metadata.
combination_rules.source_text_verbatim: CL may be appended to CP or MO when class-level information provides independent useful metadata.

combination_rules.note: CP usually contains the motif-level statement once components and modification scope are explicitly described.
combination_rules.source_text_verbatim: CP+MO is generally avoided because CP usually contains the motif-level statement once components and modification scope are explicitly described.

decision_rules.rule: Use L3-SP when a single two-dimensional constitutional structure can be proposed.
decision_rules.source_text_verbatim: Use L3-SP when a single two-dimensional constitutional structure can be proposed.

decision_rules.rule: Use L3-CP when defined molecular components, building blocks, or modifications can be proposed, but their positions, connectivities, or arrangements remain unresolved.
decision_rules.source_text_verbatim: Use L3-CP when defined molecular components, building blocks, or modifications can be proposed, but their positions, connectivities, or arrangements remain unresolved.

decision_rules.rule: Use L3-MO when only a diagnostic substructure or structural motif can be proposed without a sufficiently defined component-level representation.
decision_rules.source_text_verbatim: Use L3-MO when only a diagnostic substructure or structural motif can be proposed without a sufficiently defined component-level representation.

decision_rules.rule: Use L3-CL when the annotation is limited to a chemical or metabolite class.
decision_rules.source_text_verbatim: Use L3-CL when the annotation is limited to a chemical or metabolite class.

open_issues.title: The token CP is re-bound between versions
open_issues.detail: CP means component proposed (smb:claim/substructure_complete) in this version and class proposed (smb:claim/class) in smb-v2-consensus. Parsing CP without an explicit vocabulary version is an error, never a guess.

open_issues.title: Spectral similarity has no home in the consensus set
open_issues.detail: SM appears here as a proposed tag but was dropped from smb-v2-consensus, so migrating a reading that carries smb:evidence/spectral_similarity loses that evidence and must be marked unresolved.
